title: Startup Hiring Trends: What to Expect for August 2026
summary: Explore the key hiring trends for startups in August 2026, including fractional recruiting and AI's impact on talent acquisition.
body_text: The seed-stage founder who wants to hire a startup recruiter in 2026 is walking into a job market that looks nothing like the post-pandemic frenzy or the 2023 pullback. Capital is flowing at record levels, top talent is picky, and the way teams source and close candidates keeps tilting toward fractional work and AI support. This guide breaks down the current market so you can lock in a plan that fits your runway, your culture, and your growth goals. TLDR: Venture investment rose through Q1 2025, but boards still tie headcount to milestones, raising the quality bar on every hire. Fractional recruiters can fill three mid-level roles in a four-week sprint at around $24k, well below agency fees of 25% per placement. AI scoring tools can rank candidates and schedule outreach without a separate CRM, letting one recruiter cover more ground. AI/ML engineers command $260k to $320k in total comp in 2026; start building candidate relationships a full quarter before opening those roles. Some tools pair free ATS software with on-demand recruiting support at $75 to $125 per hour, running $2,000 to $7,000 per hire with no long-term contracts. The 2026 Hiring Market: More Capital, Sharper Strategy After two quiet years, venture investments jumped in 2024 and have continued accelerating into 2026. Crunchbase Q1 2026 funding data showed $300B flowing into 6,000 startups in Q1 2026 alone, up more than 150% year-over-year. The momentum stems from: AI hype is real: Breakthroughs in generative AI created a wave of new infrastructure startups and reopened late-stage checks. Dry-powder pressure: Funds raised in 2021 to 2022 are still expected to deploy, so investors need to place bets. Disciplined spending: Boards want headcount tied to clear milestones, so every role added must push revenue or defensibility. Early-stage teams will likely feel the pressure in two areas: Specialist roles: Machine learning, security, and revenue operations talent see multiple offers again. Budget guardrails: Even with multiple funding offers, investors favor startups with a slow burn. Founders who keep monthly cash outflow under control keep the upper hand in board conversations. “Today’s most coveted hire is the engineer who speaks product fluently. Founders who give that person fractional recruiting support win the race.” Sara Holt, Partner at Firefly Ventures Recruiting volume will not return to 2021’s spike, but the quality bar rises, while investors expect startups to have lean burn rates. In this case, teams that replace ad-hoc sourcing with data-driven funnels get ahead faster in building their dream teams. Why Fractional Recruiting Is Going Mainstream A fractional recruiter , or a fractional recruiting agency, is a seasoned pro or specialized team you hire by the hour or by the sprint. What began as a workaround for CFOs has turned into a talent-acquisition norm. Three factors explain the shift: Variable demand: Most seed and Series A startups hire in bursts, then stop. Paying a full-time recruiter during downtime is not reasonable. Network depth: Fractional recruiters often spent years at top startups or agencies and arrive with a huge network and systems in place. The best ones carry real client reviews you can read before committing hours. Cost transparency: Hourly billing opens room for transparency. A four-week sprint at $150/hour (about $24k) can fill three mid-level roles, far below the average 25% charged by agencies as fees on each $160k salary. Where the Fractional Model Works Best First GTM Build-Out : When you need an AE, SDR, and RevOps team in under 90 days, a fractional recruiter brings proven playbooks and can run the search from day one without the cost of building an internal team. One Critical Executive Hire : Agencies quote 25 to 30% for a VP or Head of Sales. A fractional partner working closely with the founder can often source and close the same talent at half that fee, with more flexibility and cost control. Post-Funding Hiring Sprint : After closing a round, you need 12+ hires in six months, then hiring slows. A fractional recruiter scales up for the sprint and back when the burst ends, without long-term overhead. A note on tools: Dover’s platform is the layer many fractional recruiting agencies run on: vetted recruiters with real client reviews plug into the free ATS in minutes, so founders get instant pipeline metrics without paying extra for software. The shared-system model matters beyond cost. When a fractional recruiter operates in a separate tool from the hiring team, candidate status and sourcing activity stay invisible until the recruiter manually sends an update. A single shared ATS gives both sides the same live view: sourcing activity, candidate stage, and outreach history are all accessible from day one. When the engagement ends, all candidate data stays in the company’s pipeline instead of leaving with the recruiter. That accumulated sourcing intelligence makes each follow-on search faster and reduces duplicated outreach to candidates who have already been contacted. How AI Tools Are Reshaping Recruiting Generative AI hit recruiting hard in 2024 and has since become table stakes. By 2026, nearly every ATS ships some form of smart ranking or writing support. But real gains come from three use cases: Resume scoring. AI scoring models read entire work histories, surface red-flag gaps, and rank matches in seconds. Dover’s AI resume scoring module, for instance, tags core skills and filters by must-have criteria automatically. Outbound sequencing. A LinkedIn sourcing extension can scrape contact data, craft a short email, and schedule follow-ups…no separate CRM needed. Predictive analytics. Time-to-fill dashboards update daily, and offer-acceptance predictions guide founders on when to offer equity or adjust start dates. Roles and Skills in High Demand Role Why Demand Spikes Typical 2026 Total Comp (US) AI/ML Engineer Product roadmaps now include embedded LLMs and custom models. $260k to $320k Infrastructure Engineer Low-latency infrastructure is needed for AI workloads and global usage. $180k to $210k Security Engineer New privacy laws and more data pipelines raise risk. $175k to $200k Full-Stack Engineer Rapid MVP iterations across web and mobile. $150k to $180k RevOps Lead Founders want every pipeline step quantified for boards. $145k to $165k Fractional Recruiter Flexible talent engine for bursts of hiring. $150 to $250/hr Source: Levels.fyi , BLS software developer wage data , Built In, salary surveys of 150 VC-backed startups. Not obvious but worth remembering: AI product managers who can talk GPU cost and brand voice will be scarce. If that role matters to your roadmap, start nurturing candidates a full quarter before you open a requisition. Mid-2026 Hiring Signals Worth Watching As of August 2026, a few patterns are shaping how seed and early-stage teams approach their next hire: AI infrastructure roles are the new DevOps. Two years ago, every startup needed a DevOps lead. Today, that same urgency applies to engineers who can build, fine-tune, and cost-manage internal AI systems. Demand outpaces supply by a wide margin, and candidates know it. Remote-first is splitting into two camps. Some well-funded teams are pulling people back to San Francisco and New York with office stipends. Others are doubling down on fully distributed models to access broader talent pools. Candidates are watching this closely before accepting offers. Boards are counting headcount in milestones, not months. The discipline from 2023 did not fully reverse when capital returned. Most Series A term sheets now include a hiring plan tied to specific product or revenue gates, so founders who show up to board meetings with a structured recruiter engagement carry more credibility than those hiring ad hoc. Fractional recruiting has moved from workaround to default. What was niche in 2022 is table stakes in 2026. Most seed-stage founders now assume their first recruiting resource will be fractional, not full-time. The question has shifted from “should we use a fractional recruiter?” to “which recruiter or fractional recruiting agency, at what hours per week, and inside which ATS?” Compensation and Flexibility in Today’s Market Salaries dropped in 2023 to 2024, but top talent in key roles still earns a premium, as recent startup role compensation benchmarks show. Equity is less predictable; some founders now offer 1-year cliffs and push refresh grants to year two, so teams stay motivated even if exits take longer. What you can expect candidates to ask for now: Hybrid autonomy: Two or three office days if travel stipends cover commuters outside core metros. Upskilling budgets: Online AI courses and conference passes rank high on wish lists. Transparent pay range: Posting the range early builds trust and speeds close rates. This saves back-and-forth on both ends. Fractional hires suit your startup best here. They weigh hourly rate, project impact, and freedom to choose clients over the above benefits. Action Checklist for Seed-to-Series B Teams Map your headcount plan in 90-day blocks so you buy the right number of recruiter hours. Draft job descriptions with salary and equity ranges up front. Set up AI scoring before the first inbound wave. Better data leads to a smoother hiring funnel. Publish a public candidate journey so applicants know what to expect. Hold a 30-minute weekly sync with your fractional recruiter and hiring managers. Track three funnel metrics: applicants per hire, onsite pass-through, and offer acceptance. Run a quarterly DEIB audit. Structured interviews and rubric scoring fight unconscious bias. How Dover Fits Into This Hiring Picture Dover is the infrastructure layer that fractional recruiting agencies are built on. The free ATS gives both the hiring team and any fractional recruiter a shared pipeline from day one: sourcing activity, candidate stage, and outreach history in one place, with all data staying on the company side when an engagement ends. Fractional recruiters in the marketplace carry real client reviews you can read before committing hours, and the model runs at $75 to $125 per hour with no long-term contracts, typically landing between $2,000 and $7,000 per hire. Whether you need just the ATS to manage inbound or a fractional recruiting agency to run a full search, the architecture is the same. The right path depends on your hiring volume, the complexity of the roles, and how much recruiting bandwidth your team can realistically carry. FAQs What is the difference between a fractional recruiter and a traditional agency? A fractional recruiter works as an hourly partner and scales up or down based on your needs. You grant them ATS access, Slack channels, and direct hiring-manager time (solved by Dover as it offers free, built-in tools to fractional recruiters). Agencies keep their own systems and only pass candidates your way. The embedded model shortens feedback loops and cuts costs. When should we hire an in-house recruiter instead? If your forecast shows at least four net new hires every month for the next year, then a full-time recruiter plus an assistant may beat hourly billing. Until then, fractional keeps overhead light. How do fractional recruiters maintain candidate quality? Reputation. They win new clients through referrals, so sending unvetted resumes harms future earnings. Many also use AI screeners and sourcing tech that outrun manual agency lists. Do I need an ATS before bringing in a fractional recruiter? An ATS handles pipeline tracking, job distribution, and applicant data storage. A fractional recruiter handles sourcing, outreach, and closing. The two are complementary layers, not substitutes. The coordination risk arises when the recruiter operates in a separate system: sourcing notes and candidate records stay with the recruiter instead of the company, and the hiring team loses visibility into what is happening between updates. A shared ATS removes that gap. Both sides see candidate status as it changes, duplicate outreach gets caught before candidates notice, and all pipeline data stays with the company when the engagement closes. Final Thoughts on Scaling Your Hiring for 2026 Companies that pair smart software with on-demand recruiting expertise can hire faster while keeping cash burn steady. The balance depends on hiring volume and role complexity: a free ATS plus the occasional fractional sprint can cover most scenarios for teams making fewer than 15 hires per year. As annual volume grows past that point, a more consistent fractional engagement often makes economic sense. Dover is one way to run that integrated model, and the platform many fractional recruiting agencies already build on: a free ATS paired with vetted recruiters carrying real client reviews, working inside the same pipeline at $75 to $125 per hour, typically running $2,000 to $7,000 per hire with no long-term contracts or placement fees, well under the SHRM 2025 average cost-per-hire of $5,475 for non-executive roles.

title: Challenges and Innovations in Alibaba's Qwen3 AI Model
summary: Explore Alibaba's Qwen3 AI model, its innovations, challenges, and how it outperforms competitors in AI technology
body_text: Artificial Intelligence evolves continuously, and companies around the globe race to push the boundaries of what these models can achieve. Alibaba's Qwen3 AI model emerges as one of the latest contenders in this technological marathon. With its innovative architecture and impressive capabilities, Qwen3 promises to be a formidable player in the AI landscape. But, like any cutting-edge technology, it presents its own set of challenges. Let's dive into the intricacies of Qwen3 and explore how it stacks up against its competitors. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Plivo (@go_plivo) Introducing Alibaba's Qwen3 AI Model Alibaba unveiled Qwen3, a new open-weight family of AI models that aims to revolutionize natural language processing and machine learning. The Qwen3 lineup includes two Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants and six dense models. This diverse range provides flexibility in applications, allowing developers to choose models that best fit their specific needs. Qwen3's top model reportedly outperforms well-known competitors like OpenAI's o1, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. This achievement is significant, considering the fierce competition in the AI field. Qwen3's performance is not just theoretical; testing has put it to the test in real-world scenarios. Qwen3 maintains the Qwen trend of massively overthinking tasks, generating thousands of thinking tokens and running out of context before answering. pic.twitter.com/mJL9ZjQtKf — Theo - t3.gg (@theo) April 28, 2025 Real-World Testing and Mixed Results In practical applications, Qwen3's 30B and 32B models have shown promising results. They have successfully passed specific tests and even generated a functional game prototype, demonstrating their potential in creative and complex tasks. These achievements highlight the model's capability to handle diverse and challenging problems, making it a versatile tool for developers. However, real-world testing reveals some mixed results. One significant issue identified is the model's tendency to overthink, consuming thousands of tokens before delivering an answer. This behavior can be inefficient, especially in time-sensitive applications where prompt responses are crucial. Additionally, during code prompts, Qwen3 repeatedly outputs "wait," which can frustrate users seeking immediate results. These issues underscore the importance of continuous refinement and highlight the challenges of developing sophisticated AI models. Qwen3-30B-A3B passes the rotating hexagon test with flying colors: To do this, it spent 11935 tokens thinking. pic.twitter.com/BYkdMkKTKf — N8 Programs (@N8Programs) April 29, 2025 Innovations and Solutions Despite these challenges, innovations within the Qwen3 model offer promising solutions. A workaround using the "/no_think" prompt effectively resolves the overthinking issue. This prompt allows users to bypass the model's tendency to overanalyze, streamlining the process and delivering faster results. The inclusion of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants in the Qwen3 family represents another innovative approach. MoE models can dynamically allocate computational resources, optimizing performance for specific tasks. This adaptability maximizes efficiency and ensures that the model can handle a wide range of applications without compromising on speed or accuracy. Qwen3 30b-a3b vs 32B on p5js animation. Generated on M3 Ultra 512 using Ollama with Q4_K_M quantized models. 30b dark background 32b light background pic.twitter.com/k9qQFmdnrC — Ivan Fioravanti ᯅ (@ivanfioravanti) April 29, 2025 Conclusion Alibaba's Qwen3 AI model represents a significant step forward in the realm of artificial intelligence. While it faces challenges such as overthinking and response delays, the innovations embedded within the model provide viable solutions. The ability to outperform established competitors and adapt to various tasks makes Qwen3 a noteworthy contender in the AI space. As we continue to explore the potential of AI, models like Qwen3 remind us of the complexities and opportunities that lie ahead. The ongoing development and refinement of such technologies shape the future of AI, impacting industries and everyday life. What do you think the next breakthrough in AI will be, and how will it change the way we interact with technology? Let's continue the conversation and explore the limitless possibilities of artificial intelligence.

title: How Quack Transforms Customer Support Across Channels
body_text: The Challenge of Modern Support Customers expect instant, reliable answers across every platform. Yet most support teams struggle with scattered tools, slow responses, and inconsistent service. A Unified Solution Quack brings every interaction into a single, easy-to-use platform. Instead of juggling multiple tools for chat, email, and social media, support teams can see the full picture in one place. This reduces the noise, ensures no customer request falls through the cracks, and allows agents to focus on solving problems rather than switching tabs. A unified view means that even if a customer moves from email to live chat or to another channel, the context is never lost—every interaction feels like part of one continuous conversation. Beyond efficiency, this unified system creates a stronger relationship between businesses and their customers. By centralizing communication, brands can apply consistent policies, tone, and response times across all channels. It also opens the door for smarter automation—like routing tickets based on urgency or customer history—without sacrificing the human touch. The result is more than just faster responses: it’s a support experience that feels personal, reliable, and built for long-term trust. Benefits That Matter Unified Inbox Every conversation, no matter the channel, appears in one streamlined workspace. Consistent Communication Built-in templates and knowledge bases ensure agents always deliver the right tone and answer. Faster Resolutions With context at their fingertips, support teams respond quicker and with fewer errors Stronger Customer Trust Nothing slips through the cracks, giving customers confidence in the service. A Real-World Example Imagine a customer starts a chat and later sends an email. With Quack, both are automatically linked. The agent sees the full history—no repeated questions, no frustration. Why This Matters Customer support has become more than just a back-office function—it is now a critical part of the brand experience. When a customer reaches out, the way a business responds shapes how they perceive the entire company. Slow replies, inconsistent answers, or missing context can quickly erode trust and push customers toward competitors. In today’s hyper-connected world, where switching services is as easy as downloading a new app, trust and responsiveness are the real differentiators. That is why building a unified, thoughtful, and efficient support system truly matters. By ensuring that no message is lost, no tone feels disconnected, and no customer is left waiting without acknowledgment, businesses show respect for their customers’ time and loyalty. It is not just about solving problems quickly—it’s about creating experiences where customers feel heard, valued, and understood. Companies that invest in this approach build relationships that last, turning everyday interactions into moments of connection that strengthen their brand at every step. Final Thought Quack replaces chaos with clarity. One platform. All channels. Seamless customer support.

body_text: La chaleur d’unités de la Plateforme Normandie de TotalEnergies est récupérée. 12 000 logements havrais sont ainsi chauffés et 16 000 tonnes de CO2 évitées. Le Havre, le 5 mai 2025 - TotalEnergies, Dalkia et la Communauté Urbaine Le Havre Seine Métropole ont inauguré l’extension du réseau de chaleur du Havre Sud, appelé RésOcéane, en présence de Jean-Baptiste Gastinne , 1er adjoint au Maire du Havre, 1er Vice-président de la Communauté urbaine Le Havre Seine Métropole, de Sylvie Jéhanno , Présidente-Directrice Générale de Dalkia, et de Jean-Marc Durand , Directeur Raffinage-Pétrochimie Europe de TotalEnergies. Engagé en février 2023, ce projet ambitieux permet de récupérer la chaleur générée par les installations du site industriel de TotalEnergies pour alimenter RésOcéane et ainsi réduire l’utilisation de gaz dans la production de chaleur. Une technologie vertueuse qui permettra de chauffer plus de 12 000 logements havrais avec une énergie locale plus propre et d’éviter l’émission de 16 000 tonnes de CO2 par an. Opéré par Dalkia, ce réseau utilise désormais 80 % de chaleur d’origine renouvelable et de chaleur industrielle récupérée. Avec ce projet inédit dans la région, l’équivalent de 80 GWh de chaleur produite par les procédés industriels de la Plateforme Normandie sont captés et valorisés. Ce projet renforce l’implication de TotalEnergies dans l’écosystème local et participe activement à l’ambition d'allier circularité et économies d'énergie, tout en contribuant aux objectifs de décarbonation du territoire et de la communauté d'agglomération du Havre. L’État, via l’ADEME, soutient les investissements relatifs à l’extension du réseau et à la distribution de la chaleur vers la ville du Havre. La récupération de la chaleur fatale de TotalEnergies est le parfait exemple de la façon dont notre métropole peut tirer parti de sa zone industrialo-portuaire pour avancer sur la voie de la transition énergétique. En raccordant la plateforme à notre réseau de chaleur urbain, nous faisons une force de notre spécificité industrielle, en explorant tous les potentiels de décarbonation , a expliqué Jean-Baptiste Gastinne, 1er adjoint au maire du Havre, 1er vice-président de la Communauté urbaine Le Havre Seine Métropole. Ce projet au Havre illustre parfaitement le potentiel de la chaleur fatale industrielle dans la décarbonation. Ce gisement énergétique encore trop peu exploité est un formidable levier pour verdir nos réseaux de chauffage urbain. L'exemple du Havre nous montre la voie à suivre, sans tarder, pour faire de la chaleur industrielle un moteur de la transition énergétique. Les solutions sont sous nos yeux, accélérons ! , a dit Sylvie Jéhanno, Présidente-Directrice Générale de Dalkia. Nous nous réjouissons d’inaugurer ce projet d’économie d’énergie ambitieux et concret. Il s’inscrit dans notre volonté de renforcer l’intégration de nos activités industrielles dans l’écosystème local. Le projet répond également à l’objectif de TotalEnergies de s’engager pour une énergie toujours plus accessible et qui inscrit la réduction des émissions de CO2 au cœur de ses projets , a déclaré Jean-Marc Durand, directeur Raffinage-Pétrochimie Europe de TotalEnergies. ***

title: Wie Sie im Jahr 2025 in der KI-Suche gut ranken: 6 Taktiken von Branchenexperten
summary: Der Suchverkehr durch KI wird die traditionelle Suche voraussichtlich bis 2028 überholen. Lernen Sie 5 bewährte Taktiken kennen, um Ihre KI-Präsenz zu verbessern.
body_text: Wir haben diesen Artikel aus dem Englischen ins Deutsche übertragen. Klicke hier , um den Originalartikel zu lesen. Wenn dir am Inhalt Probleme auffallen, schicke uns gerne eine Nachricht an report-osteam@semrush.com . Immer mehr Ihrer potenziellen Kunden nutzen KI-gestützte Suchtools wie ChatGPT, um das zu finden, was sie brauchen. Um sichtbar zu bleiben, muss Ihre Marke dort präsent sein – zusätzlich zu Ihren üblichen SEO-Maßnahmen. Tatsächlich deuten die Daten von Semrush darauf hin, dass der Traffic von großen Sprachmodellen (LLMs) den traditionellen organischen Suchverkehr bis Anfang 2028 überholen wird. Dieser Leitfaden erklärt die Grundlagen des Rankings in KI-Suchergebnissen und die Tools, mit denen Sie Ihre Inhalte für Plattformen wie ChatGPT und Googles KI-Modus optimieren können. 1. Verfolgen und vergleichen Sie Ihre KI-Präsenz Beginnen Sie mit der Analyse Ihrer aktuellen KI-Suchpräsenz , um zu sehen, was funktioniert, was verbessert werden muss und wie Sie im Vergleich zur Konkurrenz abschneiden. Das Ganze hat drei Ebenen: Ebene 1: Sichtbarkeit und Markengeschichte Dies beinhaltet, zu verstehen, welche KI-Plattformen Ihre Marke erwähnen, wie genau sie diese präsentieren und wie Sie im Vergleich zu Ihren Konkurrenten abschneiden. Alex sagte mir: „Ich möchte überprüfen, ob meine Marke und mein Produkt korrekt und einheitlich beschrieben werden.“ Ist die Stimmung positiv oder negativ? Sichtbarkeit ist nicht das einzige Ziel.“ Alex Birkett, Mitbegründer von Omniscient Digital Um dies für Ihr Unternehmen zu überprüfen, gehen Sie zum Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit , fügen Sie Ihre Domain hinzu und erkunden Sie den Bericht „ Brand Performance “. Analysieren Sie zunächst Ihren Marktanteil nach Plattform – dies ist ein Maß für Ihre Sichtbarkeit bei KI-Antworten im Vergleich zu Ihren Mitbewerbern auf Plattformen wie Google AI Mode , ChatGPT und Perplexity. Überprüfen Sie anschließend Ihren Marktanteil und Ihre Markenwahrnehmung. Hier wird angezeigt, wie häufig Sie in KI-Antworten erscheinen und ob diese Sichtbarkeit im Vergleich zu Ihren Konkurrenten positiv oder neutral dargestellt wird. Zum Schluss sollten Sie sich eingehend mit dem Abschnitt „Wichtigste Stimmungsfaktoren“ befassen, um die spezifischen Stärken und Schwächen zu verstehen, die die Markenbotschaft in KI-Antworten prägen. Dies hilft Ihnen sicherzustellen, dass die KI-Tools Ihre Marke korrekt repräsentieren. Und erkennen Sie die Lücken, die Sie schließen müssen. Schicht 2: Direkte Verkehrsbeiträge Im nächsten Schritt gilt es zu prüfen, ob KI-gestützte Zitate tatsächlich Besucher auf Ihre Website bringen. Aber Folgendes ist wichtig: Erwähnungen durch KI führen nicht immer zu sofortigem Traffic, da Nutzer möglicherweise: Klicken Sie auf keinen Fall auf die Links. Besuchen Sie uns später von einem anderen Gerät aus. Suchen Sie nach Ihrer Marke, anstatt der Quellenangabe zu folgen. Es gibt jedoch Möglichkeiten, diese Auswirkungen zu erfassen. Alex empfiehlt folgendes Vorgehen: „Analysieren Sie den Referral-Traffic, die direkten Logdateien und alle anderen Daten, die einem Klick oder Crawl von einer KI-Plattform auf Ihre Website ähneln.“ Alex Birkett, Mitbegründer von Omniscient Digital Prüfen Sie zunächst Ihre Analysedaten auf KI-spezifische Verweisquellen. Öffnen Sie in Google Analytics „ Berichte ” > „ Akquisition ” > „ Traffic-Akquise ” und ändern Sie die primäre Dimension in „ Sitzungsquelle/Medium .“ Achten Sie auf KI-spezifische Referrer wie: chatgpt.com / Empfehlung perplexity.ai / Referrer copilot.microsoft.com / Referral Sie können die Ergebnisse filtern, um diese schneller zu finden. Diese Ergebnisse geben Ihnen einen Hinweis darauf, wie viele Personen über KI-Tools auf Ihre Website gelangen. Überprüfen Sie als Nächstes Ihre Server-Logdateien. Hierbei handelt es sich um Aufzeichnungen aller Anfragen an Ihre Website. Laden Sie die Dateien von Ihrem Hosting-Anbieter oder per FTP/SFTP herunter und laden Sie sie anschließend zur einfacheren Analyse in Semrush's Log File Analyzer hoch. Öffnen Sie die neueste Protokolldatei und suchen Sie nach Benutzeragenten wie ChatGPT-User oder PerplexityBot . Dadurch wird angezeigt, wann KI-Tools Ihre Seiten besucht haben, auch wenn diese Besuche nicht in den Analysedaten erscheinen. Diese Daten sind nicht endgültig. Es kann aber zumindest anzeigen, ob diese Tools auf Ihre Website zugreifen und sie durchsuchen können. Weiterführende Informationen : Was ist eine Logdateianalyse? & So geht's für SEO Das Site-Audit-Tool kann auch KI-Crawlbarkeitsprobleme aufzeigen, um Ihnen dabei zu helfen, Probleme zu erkennen und zu beheben, die KI-Tools möglicherweise daran hindern, auf Ihre Seiten zuzugreifen oder diese zu zitieren. Ebene 3: Geschäftsauswirkungen Die dritte Ebene besteht darin, diese Aktivität mit Geschäftsergebnissen wie Demo-Anmeldungen oder Käufen zu verknüpfen. Die Nutzer sehen Ihre Marke möglicherweise in einer KI-Antwort, reagieren aber erst später, auf einem anderen Gerät oder über einen anderen Kanal. Daher ist es nicht immer möglich, KI-Suchergebnisse direkt mit Konversionen zu verknüpfen. Sie können jedoch Folgendes tun: Konversionen aus KI-gestütztem Empfehlungsverkehr verfolgen und aus direkten Traffic-Spitzen, die möglicherweise durch KI-Erwähnungen beeinflusst wurden. In Semrush können Sie außerdem KI-basierte Referral-Traffic-Widgets zu Ihren PDFs und Dashboards unter Meine Berichte hinzufügen, um die Nachverfolgung zu vereinfachen. Erhalten Sie direkte Attributions-Einblicke aus Verkaufsgesprächen indem Sie Ihren Kunden Fragen stellen wie „Wie haben Sie zum ersten Mal von uns erfahren?“ oder „Was hat Sie dazu veranlasst, mit uns Kontakt aufzunehmen?“ „Einen erheblichen Teil unserer Leads erhalten wir durch Erwähnungen auf ChatGPT.“ Erst gestern hatte ich ein Verkaufsgespräch, bei dem die potenzielle Kundin ihren Bildschirm teilte und mir genau die Suchbegriffe zeigte, mit denen sie uns gefunden hatte.“ Alex Birkett, Mitbegründer von Omniscient Digital 2. Markenautorität aufbauen und dort präsent sein, wo es darauf ankommt. Wenn Ihre Marke im Internet bekannt ist und darüber gesprochen wird, ist es viel wahrscheinlicher, dass sie in KI-generierten Antworten auftaucht. Untersuchungen von Kevin Indig zeigen, dass das Suchvolumen einer Marke der stärkste Indikator für Markenerwähnungen in KI-Chatbots ist – insbesondere in ChatGPT. Aber es geht nicht nur darum, bekannt zu sein. Man muss auch an den richtigen Orten präsent sein – und aus den richtigen Gründen zitiert werden. Hier sind einige effektive Taktiken, die Ihnen dabei helfen und Ihre Markenpräsenz erhöhen können: Gastbeitrag in renommierten Publikationen damit Ihr Name und Ihre Expertise in vertrauenswürdigen Quellen erscheinen, auf die sich LLMs beziehen können. Arbeiten Sie mit Branchenexperten zusammen bei Webinaren, Berichten oder gemeinsamen Forschungsprojekten, die natürliche KI-Erwähnungen erzielen. Veröffentlichen Sie datenbasierte Studien, die andere in Ihrer Nische in ihren eigenen Arbeiten zitieren und verlinken können. Verwende deine stärksten Inhalte in verschiedenen Formaten (wie Artikeln, Podcasts und Videos), damit sie in mehr Quellen gefunden werden können, auf die KI-Tools zugreifen können. HubSpot hat beispielsweise eine große, von Experten betreute Inhaltsbibliothek zu den Themen Vertrieb, Marketing und KI aufgebaut. Die Inhalte kombinieren originelle Meinungen, Dateneinblicke und kostenlose Tools. Dieser Inhalt bietet einen einzigartigen Mehrwert und wird von der Community häufig geteilt, referenziert und erwähnt. HubSpot verfügt außerdem über ein eigenes aktives Subreddit mit 14.000 Mitgliedern: Das Ergebnis? Die Marke rangiert regelmäßig an der Spitze bei KI-gestützten Suchanfragen mit hoher Suchintention zu Themen wie CRM und Marketingautomatisierung. 3. Strukturieren Sie Ihre Inhalte für die KI-Extraktion Wenn Sie Ihre Inhalte so strukturieren, dass sie leicht lesbar und verständlich sind, erhöhen Sie auch Ihre Chancen, in KI-generierte Antworten aufgenommen zu werden. Warum? Denn KI-Systeme lesen nicht nur Wörter, sondern interpretieren den Kontext. Die Art und Weise, wie Sie Ihre Inhalte strukturieren, vermittelt den Lesern, was wichtig ist und wie die Ideen miteinander verbunden sind. Anschließend nutzen sie diesen Kontext, um ihre Antworten auf Benutzeranfragen zu formulieren. Um dies in die Praxis umzusetzen: Verwenden Sie eine klare Überschriftenhierarchie (H2s, H3s usw.), um Themengrenzen zu definieren und das Scannen für KI-Tools (und Benutzer) zu erleichtern. Schreiben Sie kurze, einfache Sätze , die klare Verbindungen zwischen den verschiedenen Konzepten herstellen, die Sie besprechen. Fügen Sie semantisches HTML und Schema-Markup (wie FAQPage, HowTo und Review) hinzu, um maschinenlesbaren Kontext bereitzustellen. Platzieren Sie Ihre Antworten gleich zu Beginn , damit die wichtigsten Informationen frühzeitig angezeigt werden. Verwenden Sie prägnante Formate wie Stichpunkte, Tabellen und Frage-Antwort-Blöcke&, um es KI-Tools zu erleichtern, Antworten aus Ihren Inhalten zu extrahieren. Zum Beispiel dieser Semrush-Artikel über Googles KI-Modus beginnt mit einer klaren Überschrift, die als Frage formuliert ist. Unmittelbar darauf folgt dann eine kurze, direkte Antwort. Der Artikel verwendet außerdem vergleichende Tabellen, die wichtige Informationen übersichtlich und strukturiert darstellen, sodass KI-Systeme diese leicht übernehmen und in ihren Antworten verwenden können. Schließlich enthält es Überschriften in Form von Fragen, gefolgt von prägnanten Antworten, bevor es ins Detail geht. Dies spiegelt den Q&A-Stil wider, den KI-Modelle leicht erkennen können. All dies trägt dazu bei, dass die Inhalte mit größerer Wahrscheinlichkeit in KI-Tools wie ChatGPT zitiert werden: 4. Aktualisieren Sie Ihre Inhalte regelmäßig. LLM-Absolventen bevorzugen eindeutig Inhalte, die kürzlich veröffentlicht oder aktualisiert wurden. Daher ist es ratsam, Ihre Inhalte regelmäßig zu überprüfen und zu aktualisieren. Und fast 90 % davon befanden sich auf Seiten, die in den letzten drei Jahren aktualisiert worden waren. Nur 6 % der Zugriffe erfolgten auf Inhalte, die älter als 6 Jahre waren. Um Ihre Inhalte effektiv aktuell zu halten, konzentrieren Sie sich auf sinnvolle Aktualisierungen, die Relevanz und Genauigkeit priorisieren: Ersetzen Sie veraltete Zahlen durch die neuesten Studien, Berichte und Benchmarks. Fügen Sie neue Beispiele oder Fallstudien hinzu, die aktuelle Branchenveränderungen, Produkteinführungen oder Erfolgsgeschichten hervorheben. Neue Tools, Strategien oder Praktiken vorstellen, nach denen Ihre Zielgruppe sucht Defekte oder veraltete Links reparieren und sicherstellen, dass alle externen Verweise noch gültig und vertrauenswürdig sind Neuoptimierung für Keywords und Inhaltsstruktur zur Anpassung an die aktuelle Suchnachfrage und KI-Vorschläge Diagramme, Screenshots und Grafiken aktualisieren , damit sie die aktuellen Benutzeroberflächen und Daten widerspiegeln. Ich habe den Ablauf verbessert, neue Beispiele und Statistiken hinzugefügt und neue Trends wie den Einsatz von KI berücksichtigt. Daher erkennen KI-Tools wie Perplexity dies nun bei relevanten Anfragen: Dies trägt dazu bei, dass Semrush bei SaaS-Unternehmen, die ihre Content-Programme ausbauen möchten, stets präsent bleibt. 5. Erstellen Sie Inhalte basierend auf echten Kundenfragen Eine weitere wirkungsvolle Methode, um Ihre Sichtbarkeit in der KI-Suche zu steigern, besteht darin, Seiten zu erstellen, die direkt die tatsächlichen Fragen Ihrer Kunden beantworten. Warum? Weil KI-Tools es Nutzern ermöglichen, hochspezifische und detaillierte Fragen zu stellen – viel detaillierter als Ihre typischen SEO-Keywords . Um diese Anfragen aufzudecken, beginnen Sie mit der Analyse Ihrer First-Party-Daten . Dies umfasst Verkaufsgespräche und Demo-Transkripte, Kundensupport-Tickets, Chat-Protokolle und sogar Daten der Google Search Console zu markenbezogenen Keywords. Diese offenbaren oft: Wiederholte Fragen Einwände Vergleiche mit Wettbewerbern Fragen der Art „Wie mache ich…“ oder „Warum funktioniert das nicht…“ Abgesehen von Ihren eigenen Daten können Ihnen Foren und Social-Media-Plattformen dabei helfen zu verstehen, wie Ihre Zielkunden tatsächlich über ihre Herausforderungen sprechen. Schließlich heben spezialisierte Tools zur Optimierung generativer Engines (GEO) wie das AI Visibility Toolkit von Semrush die Fragen hervor, die KI-Engines am häufigsten stellen. Sie konzentrierten sich auf Suchanfragen, bei denen die Marke entweder keine starke Platzierung erreichte oder im Vergleich zu anderen Nischenanbietern gar nicht vertreten war. Anschließend erstellte das Chargeblast-Team auf Basis dieser Daten einen vollständigen Content-Plan und begann mit der Erstellung von Inhalten, um die Lücken zu schließen. „Mithilfe der Anregungen aus dem AI Visibility Toolkit haben wir zielgerichtete Blog-Inhalte erstellt, die diesen Möglichkeiten gerecht werden.“ Wir versuchen, bei Anfragen zum Thema Rückbuchungen eine Vorreiterrolle einzunehmen, indem wir unsere Content-Strategie an den tatsächlichen Fragen der Nutzer auf KI-Plattformen ausrichten.“ Anj Viray, Marketingleiterin bei Chargeblast Das Unternehmen fand relevante Anfragen wie „Gibt es Chargeback-Lösungen speziell für abonnementbasierte Unternehmen?“ und fügte neue Seiten hinzu, die auf jede dieser Anfragen abzielten: 6. Nutzen Sie Video als Magnet für Zitate Das Veröffentlichen qualitativ hochwertiger YouTube-Videos kann Ihnen auch helfen, in KI-generierten Antworten zitiert zu werden. Daten von Semrush zeigen, dass YouTube die dritthäufigst genannte Domain in KI-Antworten ist. Videos werden häufig in Tools wie ChatGPT und insbesondere in Google AI Overviews für Informationsanfragen verwendet. Um mit Videos erfolgreich zu sein, konzentrieren Sie sich auf die bereits identifizierten, realen Kundenfragen und nutzen Sie Formate wie: Anleitungen : Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitungen, die einen Prozess erläutern und einen Mehrwert bieten (z. B. „So erstellen Sie eine E-Mail-Nurturing-Sequenz in HubSpot“) Visuelle Demos : Ein Produkt, ein Workflow oder eine Technik wird in Aktion gezeigt, um genau zu veranschaulichen, wie es funktioniert (z. B. „Einen Shopify-Shop in weniger als 30 Minuten einrichten“) Vergleiche und Bewertungen : Bietet detaillierte Gegenüberstellungen, die entscheidungsorientierte Fragen beantworten (z. B. „Mailchimp vs. ActiveCampaign: Welches passt besser zu einem kleinen Unternehmen?“). Weiterführende Literatur : Videomarketing: Der ultimative Leitfaden für 2025 Setzen Sie diese Taktiken ein, um in den Suchergebnissen der KI besser platziert zu werden. Die KI-Suche entwickelt sich schnell zu einer bevorzugten Methode für Menschen, um Antworten und Produkte zu finden. Das bedeutet, dass die Platzierung in den Antworten von KI-Tools auf die Fragen Ihrer Zielgruppe ein wichtiger Faktor ist: Bleiben Sie wettbewerbsfähig. Bleiben Sie im Bewusstsein Ihrer Zielgruppe präsent. Steigern Sie den Umsatz Ihres Unternehmens Mit dem AI Visibility Toolkit von Semrush lassen sich KI-Suchrankings einfach überwachen und optimieren. Probieren Sie es noch heute aus und verbessern Sie die Sichtbarkeit Ihrer KI-Marke. title: Oblivious Is Not Always Private
summary: Learn how Tinfoil compares to Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) and what the right solution is for AI applications requiring data privacy.
body_text: ← Back to Posts Oblivious Is Not Always Private May 10, 2025 • 6 min read Sacha Servan-Schreiber Introduction As AI systems process more and more sensitive personal information, companies have started developing "private" AI offerings of various sorts. In this blog post, we unpack what privacy means in the context of AI applications. In particular, we will focus on why Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) — a new Internet protocol pioneered by Apple and Cloudflare for anonymity on the web — is often not the right tool for AI privacy. As demand for privacy in AI applications continues to grow, especially in enterprise contexts, we see different definitions of privacy emerge from AI providers. For some AI providers, "privacy" merely means vague promises like "we don't train on your data"; while saying nothing about other ways they might use your data. Others might claim privacy by using OHTTP, a protocol designed to decouple user identity from web requests. OHTTP is an excellent tool for identity protection and a critical component in many web-based systems. However, it's important to understand its specific design purpose, design context, and limitations when applied to AI systems. In particular, OHTTP was designed for identity anonymization (hiding IP addresses) when performing web requests. It was not designed for applications where data privacy is needed. As such, it fails to provide meaningful privacy when it comes to AI applications, as we explain next. Understanding OHTTP: Protecting Who, Not What OHTTP decouples user identity from web request content. It works by routing encrypted Internet requests and responses through a relay that sits between the client and its destination, separating who initiated the request from what was sent in the request. This provides unlinkability (i.e., anonymity) by hiding the user's IP address from the service provider. How OHTTP Works OHTTP functions a bit like a VPN by hiding the user's identity from the destination server. However, unlike VPNs, where the VPN service knows both the client identity and the destination, OHTTP proxies the connection through two non-colluding entities called a Relay and a Gateway. This ensures that the first entity (the Relay, which sees the client IP address) does not see the content of the request. Similarly, the second entity (the Gateway, which decrypts and processes the request) does not know the source of the connection. OHTTP provides identity unlinkability, not data privacy While OHTTP prevents linking the user identity to requests, it is important to understand that it only protects who sent the data, not the data itself from the destination server. This works great for applications with fixed transactional requests that reveal information over time through metadata, such as DNS queries or telemetry reporting. In particular, OHTTP is designed for either accessing publicly available content (such as a DNS record) or sending generic data such as a crash report that does not contain personally-identifiable information (PII). However, when personal data is present in the request, all bets are off. OHTTP + AI ≠ Privacy For AI applications processing emails, documents, or other content containing sensitive data or PII, this creates a big problem: Once decrypted at the destination, the actual content (including any PII) is fully exposed to the receiving server. If your data contains identifying information (like your name), OHTTP does not provide any meaningful privacy guarantees, since the PII is linked to your identity! It's analogous to wearing a hood and mask to protect your identity and then pinning your ID to your forehead. So is OHTTP Useful? Yes! OHTTP is a critical component of a comprehensive Internet privacy solution. In many situations, the unlinkability property achieved by OHTTP is vital in preventing ISPs and other network observers from potentially learning sensitive information about you. For example, using OHTTP prevents ISPs from learning your browsing history or Apple from learning which applications you're running through crash reports and other telemetry sent from your devices. However, neither of these contexts involve sending over personal information that can be linked back to you. For AI applications, we cannot assume that conversations and other queries are free of PII. Copy-pasting an email from your boss into ChatGPT? That contains PII and even potentially proprietary company information. In this case, ChatGPT can link the request back to you, regardless of whether you anonymized the connection through OHTTP. To have privacy in such cases, we need a stronger property: data privacy. Tinfoil Privacy: Protecting the Data Itself Tinfoil provides actual data privacy through secure enclaves. Tinfoil protects code and data inside the enclave with privacy and integrity. Data privacy guarantees that only the inference logic ever has access to the data, and that all entities (including Tinfoil) outside the secure enclave environment never see your data. How Tinfoil protects your privacy Secure enclaves provide an isolated, protected environment within the processor for sensitive operations. This isolation is enforced at the hardware level, ensuring neither the operating system nor other applications can access data being processed within the enclave. The secure enclave uses hardware-based memory encryption to isolate specific application code and data in memory. You can learn more about how Tinfoil uses secure hardware enclaves in our other blog post where we provide a technical overview. For AI applications processing personal data, secure enclaves protect the data during use . This means personal data remains encrypted even in memory during processing, allowing Tinfoil to run AI models in the cloud while maintaining full confidentiality of the data. Conclusion As AI increasingly processes sensitive personal information, understanding the distinction between privacy technologies is crucial. OHTTP (and even VPNs) can create the illusion of privacy by hiding your IP address, but they are not designed to protect your data from the service provider. It is easy to shoot yourself in the foot by assuming that network-level anonymity also means your data stays private from the processor. For users trusting AI systems with sensitive information — whether it's proprietary code, work emails, or personal documents — confidential computing or fully on-prem deployments are the only solutions that guarantee privacy regardless of the data you feed into the AI system. You can always use OHTTP in conjunction with Tinfoil to hide your IP address from us, but regardless of whether or not you use OHTTP, we never see your data. As AI systems become more integrated into our professional and personal lives, the question isn't just "Does anyone know I used this service?" but rather "Can anyone see what I shared with this service?" For true privacy in AI applications deployed on the cloud, confidential computing needs to be part of the picture. summary: How we leverage our success and engineering relationship to improve customer experience.
body_text: The quality of any product is in the details. And yet we noticed a pattern. Our support team would bring up a small bug and it would get lost in the flood of new features. Even when Support contacted Engineering, no one would own the request, and so it would often go untracked. Prioritizing fixing small bugs, improving UX, or polishing details can often get lost in the desire to ship new features. The Problems We noticed at least two problems occurring regularly. Either genuine needs would go unaddressed because we were busy developing new features or our engineers lost the ability to tackle more focus-intensive projects due to requests to address bugs. Each problem has its own set of short-term and long-term consequences. The Principles As with many problems, it's important to work from your principles to the proper solution. We identified three key principles: Quality over features : Our commitment to quality is our top priority and is a key differentiator. Collaboration and communication : Effective communication and collaboration within our team and across departments are crucial for resolving issues efficiently. Customer-centric approach : Our primary focus is on delivering a delightful experience to customers. The Solution While we encourage all our engineers to stay in touch with the needs of Resend users, our Support team lives the day-to-day with our customers. We found the solution to small bug fixes and improvements by leveraging the relationship between Support and Engineering. Internally strengthening that team relationship led to an improved customer experience. We developed a new rotating role called " The Fixer ." The Fixer plays a critical role within Resend, ensuring that our products maintain high quality and reliability. The Implementation Each week, we assign an engineering team member the role of "Fixer". The rotation ensures every engineer empathizes with support and can effectively contribute to resolving issues. We use Incident.io to create our rotation schedule and automatically update @the-fixer tag in Slack with the assigned engineer. We track Fixer tasks using a few tools: Slack : all bugs and improvements are posted on our #all-triage channel and tagging @the-fixer contacts the assigned engineer Linear : we track each ticket on our Customer Engineering board and use the-fixer label to auto-apply a 14-day SLA to ensure we fix the bug within two weeks. While the Fixer is ultimately responsible for addressing the bugs raised, they'll often need more context on an issue or help finding a fix, so others are brought in as needed. Care and attention to user needs is a core value at Resend. We even celebrated the role by creating a custom enamel pin for the Fixer to give to our engineers. The Benefits We immediately noticed several benefits both internally and externally. Cross-team collaboration: this structure has improved the collaboration between Success (or whoever is reporting the bug) and Engineering Bug ownership : assigning an owner for reported bugs provides clarity for each issue Deep focus : while other engineers do help address bugs regularly, not being the Fixer allows for deeper focus on more complex problems and roadmap features Timely response : the system lets us track report-to-fix and enables us to circle back around to customers with confidence Shared responsibility : it's easy to build features in a vacuum, but the Fixer's close connection to customers ensures engineering stays in contact with real customers and that each engineer retains context on the whole product We're excited to continue to improve our processes and better serve our customers.

title: Scaling life sustainably by unlocking space mobility
summary: Humanity’s population has grown at an extraordinary pace, pushing us closer to — and potentially beyond — the Earth’s environmental carrying capacity: the maximum number of people our planet can support without causing lasting harm to...
body_text: Humanity’s population has grown at an extraordinary pace, pushing us closer to — and potentially beyond — the Earth’s environmental carrying capacity: the maximum number of people our planet can support without causing lasting harm to the environment. As we continue to scale our civilization, we face a pressing question: how do we do so without compromising the health of our planet? Addressing this challenge requires innovation in multiple areas. We must develop sustainable solutions for clean energy, water access, resource extraction, waste management, atmospheric stability, and more. A holistic, multipronged approach is essential — and a thriving, sustainable space economy must be a key part of that strategy. Achieving this will depend on routine, low-cost access to a wide range of orbits — designed from the start to be both scalable and environmentally sustainable. LKQ Europe chief calls for aftermarket experiences for critical MVBER review
summary: LKQ Europe chief calls for aftermarket experiences for critical MVBER review
body_text: Zug, Switzerland. LKQ Europe's President and Executive Managing Director, Andy Hamilton, has called on the automotive aftermarket to provide real-world evidence of market barriers as the European Commission collects comments for its public consultation on Motor Vehicle Block Exemption Regulations (MVBER). The LKQ Europe chief is calling all independent garages and workshops to share their experiences of barriers to repair, service, or maintenance, which will form part of the company's submission to the Commission's consultation. These could include instances of denied access to technical information, excessive charges for diagnostic data, or warranty-related obstacles. LKQ has highlighted three key areas where the current regulations, implemented in 2023, need strengthening to ensure fair competition in the automotive aftermarket sector, which will form part of its response to the consultation. Andy Hamilton, President and Executive Managing Director, said : "While the current MVBER represented significant progress, we're already seeing gaps emerge in the framework as vehicle technology rapidly evolves. We continue to see cases where workshops are forced to jump through unnecessary hoops to access basic diagnostic information or are charged excessive fees for data that should be readily available. “Warranty transparency remains a problem. Too many customers still believe incorrectly that their vehicle warranty will be invalidated if they use an independent workshop. “Critically, we need to address access to in-vehicle data now, not later - by the time the newest vehicles reach the independent aftermarket in 5-10 years, it will be too late to retrofit solutions. Independent workshops shouldn't have to resort to expensive court battles to assert rights that are already enshrined in law." The LKQ Europe leader also focused on enforcement mechanisms, with Hamilton citing the recent European Court of Justice case between Fiat and Carglass/ATU over diagnostic port access as an example of the challenges faced by independent operators. Industry stakeholders are encouraged to submit their experiences through organizations including LKQ Europe, FIGIEFA, ADPA, and CECRA to help build a comprehensive case for enhanced protections and more effective enforcement mechanisms in the next iteration of MVBER. To share with LKQ Europe, contact communications@lkqeurope.com . About LKQ Europe LKQ Europe, a subsidiary of LKQ Corporation ( www.lkqcorp.com ), headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, is the leading distributor of automotive aftermarket parts for cars, commercial vans, and industrial vehicles in Europe. It currently employs approximately 26,500 people with a network of more than 900 branches and approximately $6.4 billion in revenue in 2024. The organization supplies more than 100,000 workshops in over 18 European countries in the following regions: Benelux-France, Central Eastern Europe, DACH, Italy, Scandinavia and UK & Ireland.
